facts.fact: Orbit Media's annual blogger survey found that bloggers who update old articles were twice as likely to report strong results from content marketing (third-party claim cited by Adwave).
facts.quote: bloggers who update old articles were **twice as likely** to report “strong results” from content marketing

facts.fact: Search Engine People identifies pages ranking in positions 11 to 30 in Google as the best candidates for an update (third-party recommendation cited by Adwave).
facts.quote: Search Engine People highlights pages ranking in **positions 11 to 30** as the best candidates for an update

facts.fact: Lotus Optimisation recommends keeping title tags near 60 characters (third-party guidance cited by Adwave).
facts.quote: It also recommends keeping **title tags near 60 characters**

facts.fact: Lotus Optimisation recommends keeping meta descriptions around 140 to 160 characters (third-party guidance cited by Adwave).
facts.quote: **meta descriptions around 140 to 160 characters** to stay click-worthy in search results

facts.fact: Adwave defines striking-distance posts as posts that rank on page two or three in search results for terms that matter to the business.
facts.quote: **Striking-distance posts**. These rank on page two or three for terms that matter to the business.

facts.fact: The page cites practitioner guidance suggesting refreshed blog posts target 1,500 to 2,000 words to better match competitive SERP depth.
facts.quote: Practitioner guidance suggests targeting **1,500 to 2,000 words** to better match competitive SERP depth

facts.fact: The page cites Faith Hanan's guidance on blog updates as recommending the main keyword appear in at least one-third of H2 headings but no more than 60%.
facts.value: at least 33% (one-third) and no more than 60%
facts.quote: keeping the main keyword in **at least one-third of H2 headings, but no more than 60%**

facts.fact: The page recommends reviewing refreshed pages' results 30, 60, and 90 days after publication to decide whether to optimize again, promote harder, or leave the page alone.
facts.quote: They look at results 30, 60, and 90 days after publication, then decide whether to optimize again, promote harder, or leave the page alone.
